items.original: Exercise9.34 states that the source type must be a class ancestor or descendant of the cast target, without separating interface-typed operands.
items.correction: For concrete class types use the single-inheritance ancestry test. An interface-typed operand may hold an implementing class object; preserve that case with runtime checks rather than reject it as unrelated ancestry.
items.basis: Original9.34 and definitions9.5.1/fig9.12 read; interface I argument containing class A cast to A tested, alongside sibling-class rejection.

items.original: Runtime apply-method uses empty-env while the displayed typechecker check-method-decl uses init-tenv.
items.correction: The companion uses the same parameter/field/static base in runtime and typechecking; main initial variables do not become free bindings in methods.
items.basis: Both original figures visually read; a method with unbound x is rejected while a field named x remains valid.

items.original: The source send clause uses parallel Scheme let bindings; figure9.8 and several class/interface examples are schematic or require explicit clients.
